chart.hint: Hover the chart, or focus it and use the arrow keys, to read a value.

overview.title: Traffic, {{window}}
overview.sources: Requests and tokens come from the usage ledger. Failed requests and latency come from the trace buffer, which keeps only the most recent requests.
overview.capped: The trace buffer reports at most 7 days, so failed requests and latency cover the last 7 days.
overview.emptyText: This page fills in after the first request. Send one from Chat, or call the API from your own client.
overview.scrape: Scrape the same numbers into your own Prometheus or Grafana from /metrics.

figures.unknown: The trace buffer could not be read

charts.failedOff: Failed requests are known only while tracing is on.
charts.noTraces: No traced request in this window.

usage.title: Usage, {{window}}
usage.sourceAdmin: Every user's requests and tokens, from the usage ledger. The ledger records tokens and requests by model, user and API key. It does not record status, endpoint or node.
usage.sourceOwn: Your own requests and tokens, from the usage ledger.
usage.pricingNote: An estimate from the prices you type here. The prices stay in this browser and apply to recorded token counts. LocalAI has no price of its own.
usage.emptyText: Usage appears here as API requests are made.
usage.noMatchText: Clear the search or the model filter to see every row.
usage.projectedLine: about {{value}} tokens by the end of the window if the trend holds (a straight line)
usage.projected: If the trend holds, about {{value}} tokens by the end of the window (a straight line through the buckets so far).

quota.runsOut: Runs out in {{time}} at this pace

usage.caption: Usage by {{group}}
usage.noSeries: No time series for this row.
usage.noEndpoint: Rows by endpoint, by node or by status are not offered: the usage ledger does not record them. Requests by status are in Traces.

models.title: Models
models.sources: Requests and tokens over the {{window}} come from the usage ledger. Operations and errors come from the backend-operation buffer. Memory is what the backend process holds now. LocalAI keeps no per-model latency percentile or memory history.
models.caption: Models with their requests, tokens and backend operations
models.emptyText: Models appear here once they are installed or used.
models.noBuffer: The backend-operation buffer is not available (backend logging is off).
models.noReading: The server reports no reading for this model.
models.memoryNote: Memory held is the resident host memory of the backend process, when the server reports it. GPU memory per model is not reported.
models.bufferNote: Operations and errors count the {{count}} operations the buffer still holds, not all time.

host.title: GPU and host
host.sources: The current reading from the server, refreshed every 5 seconds. LocalAI reports memory per GPU, system memory, the CPU share and the models disk. It does not report GPU utilisation or temperature.
host.waiting: The chart starts with the second reading, about 5 seconds after you open this page.
host.error: The host could not be read. {{message}}
host.noGpu: No GPU is reported. Models run on the CPU and system memory.
host.notReported: Not reported by LocalAI: GPU utilisation, GPU temperature, power, and any history. The charts below are this page's own readings.
host.noMemory: No memory reading is available, so no chart is drawn.
host.cpuSub: since you opened this page, at most 240 readings
host.lostNodes: A node that stops answering keeps its last reading and is marked in the State column. A node that reports no memory shows no reading.

traces.title: Traces
traces.noMatchText: Clear the search or pick All to see every trace in the buffer.
traces.noneText: Traces appear here as API requests are made.
traces.offText: LocalAI records no request while tracing is off, so there are no failed requests, latency or trace pages to show. Turn it on to record requests, responses and backend operations.
traces.backendNoneText: Backend operations appear here as models run.
traces.backendOffText: Turn on backend logging in the settings above to capture per-model process output.
traces.bufferNote: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} in the trace buffer. The buffer keeps only the most recent requests.

settings.notRecorded: new requests will not be recorded
settings.enableHint: Record API requests, responses, and backend operations
settings.maxItemsHint: Maximum trace items to retain (0 = unlimited)
settings.maxBodyHint: Per-field cap for captured bodies and backend trace data (0 = uncapped). Keeps oversized LLM histories or TTS snippets from locking this page.
settings.loggingHint: Capture backend process output per model, without requiring debug mode

trace.missingTitle: This trace is no longer in the buffer
trace.missingText: The buffer keeps only the most recent requests, and a restart clears it. Open the list for what it holds now.
trace.errorTitle: The trace could not be read
trace.whyRunning: The request is still running. It has no result yet.
trace.whyError: The server answered {{status}} and recorded this error:
trace.whyStatus: The server answered {{status}} and recorded no error text.
trace.whyRefused: The server refused the request with status {{status}}. LocalAI does not count a 4xx status as a failed request.
trace.whyNote: This is what the trace buffer holds. LocalAI records no cause beyond the status and the error text.
trace.opBar: {{type}} started {{offset}} after the request began and took {{time}}
trace.timelineMatched: The operations under the request are backend operations that ran while it was open, matched on time and model. The API and backend buffers share no request id.
trace.timelineNone: No backend operation was recorded while this request was open.
trace.noBodyText: No body was kept for this request.
trace.hidden: Hidden until you reveal it: bodies can hold prompts and personal data.
trace.truncated: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}}: the body was capped when it was recorded.

audio.title: Audio Snippet
audio.truncated: Audio clip not playable. It was truncated when recorded (raise Max Body Bytes in the tracing settings).

middleware.title: Middleware
middleware.lede: What a request passes through, in this order.
middleware.orderNote: Select a step to see only its rules. The server fixes the order and it cannot be rearranged.
middleware.piiIntro: Redaction is per model and runs on the request. It is off by default. Backends that match
middleware.piiIntro2: default to on (cloud passthroughs). A model opts in with pii.enabled and a list of detectors, and each detector is a token_classify model whose pii_detection block sets the policy.
middleware.noopTitle: Enabled but no detector resolved, so nothing is scanned. Switch on a detector's Default below, or add pii.detectors to the model.
middleware.addDetectorTitle: Add a NER or pattern detector model
middleware.detectorsIntro: These token_classify models do the scanning. Switch Default on to apply a detector to any PII-enabled model that names none of its own, mostly cloud-proxy and TLS-proxy models. A model's own pii.detectors always wins.
middleware.missingDetector: This default detector names a model that is not loaded.
middleware.noDetectors: No detector models loaded. Add one with the button above (a token_classify NER model or a built-in secret pattern model).
middleware.cachedDecision: Cached decision. Per-label scores are not recorded: the cache stores only the resulting label set.
middleware.fallbackDecision: Out-of-corpus fallback. The nearest labelled corpus entry was at similarity {{value}}, below the router's gate. Seed examples near this kind of prompt to route it.
middleware.noScores: No per-label scores were recorded for this decision (likely a fallback row).
middleware.activation: Activation threshold {{value}}%. The marker on each bar shows it.
middleware.noRoutersText: Add a router block to a model YAML to enable routing. The classifier picks one of the listed candidates for each request, and the usual model resolution then runs on the chosen target.
middleware.addRouterTitle: Open the model editor with the Routing Model template
middleware.routersNote: Edit the router model's YAML to change candidates or rules.
middleware.noDecisions: No routing decisions yet. Send a request to a router model to fill this log.
middleware.label: Label
middleware.expand: Click to see the per-label score breakdown
middleware.proxyUnavailableText: The status endpoint did not return a proxy section.
middleware.conflictTitle: TLS proxy disabled: duplicate host claims
middleware.conflictText: Each intercept host must be owned by exactly one model config. Edit the conflicting model YAML files to resolve it.
middleware.proxyIntro: The TLS proxy terminates TLS for allowlisted hosts so PII redaction can run on traffic from clients that sign in with OAuth or a subscription (Claude Code, Codex CLI). Other hosts get a plain CONNECT tunnel with no inspection and no CA trust needed.
middleware.hostsClaimed: Hosts claimed by model configs (PII settings come from the owning config):
middleware.noHosts: No model config declares an intercept host. Without one, every CONNECT tunnels through unchanged. Create one from the Add Model page with the MITM Intercept template.
middleware.noCa: The CA is not generated yet. Start the listener to generate it.
middleware.addProxyModelTitle: Open the model editor with the MITM Intercept template
middleware.noProxyModels: No model config declares mitm.hosts. Use Add MITM model: the template defaults to api.anthropic.com with PII filtering on.
middleware.listenHint: Bind address for the proxy listener. Empty disables it. Bind to 127.0.0.1:port unless only clients you control can reach it: the CONNECT port has no auth. Clients connect to the proxy over plain HTTP (use http://, even in HTTPS_PROXY), and the proxy terminates TLS for allowlisted hosts inside the tunnel.
middleware.interceptNote: Intercept hosts are declared per model in the model YAML under mitm.hosts. Each host is owned by one model config, and PII filtering and pattern overrides come from that config.
middleware.setup2: Trust it on the client. For Node-based CLIs (Claude Code, Codex):
middleware.setup3: Point the client at the proxy:
middleware.setup3b: (yes, http://: clients speak plain HTTP to the proxy, which then terminates TLS for allowlisted hosts on the inner connection).
middleware.admissionText: Requests over a key's rate limit or a quota are refused before they reach a model. Limits are set per user and key. LocalAI shows the refusals below as events, and has no list of admission rules to show here.
middleware.admissionNone: No refusal in the recent events.
middleware.eventsSub: shared by the PII filter, the proxy and admission, newest first, capped at 100
middleware.subject: Subject
middleware.noEventsText: Events appear when a PII detector flags an entity, when the proxy decides whether to intercept a hostname, or when an intercepted request finishes. Request bodies are never stored. Use the API and backend traces for those.
middleware.knnEmptyTitle: Seed labelled example prompts via POST /api/router/{name}/corpus. Every request falls back until the corpus has entries near it.
middleware.knnTitle: {{total}} labelled examples; the {{k}} nearest vote; entries below similarity {{sim}} cannot vote (prompts outside the corpus use the fallback)

prometheus.title: Prometheus
prometheus.lede: LocalAI exposes metrics in the Prometheus text format. Scrape them into your own Prometheus or Grafana.
prometheus.auth: GET /metrics is admin only. Give your scraper an admin API key as a Bearer token. The route does not exist when LocalAI runs with LOCALAI_DISABLE_METRICS_ENDPOINT.

scrape.ok_one: This server answers. It exposes {{count}} metric family.
scrape.ok_other: This server answers. It exposes {{count}} metric families.
scrape.off: This server does not serve /metrics. Metrics are switched off.
scrape.denied: This server refused the request. The route needs an admin account.

metric.apiCall: Request duration in seconds, by HTTP method and route. The only metric that is always on.
metric.tokens: Tokens accounted, by user, served model and kind (prompt or completion).
metric.billed: Requests accounted, by user, served model and endpoint.
metric.cost: Cost accounted in USD, by user and served model.
metric.unrecorded: Requests that finished but produced no usage record. A rising count means a gap in accounting.
metric.pii: PII and audit events, by kind, origin, action and direction.
metric.failoverUp: 1 when a failover target is healthy, 0 when it is not.
metric.compressionEvents: Chat context compression attempts, by model and result.
metric.prefixCache: Prefix-cache forced-disturb events started by this frontend.

prometheus.conditional: Only api_call is always present. The others appear while the feature behind them runs, so "not seen yet" is not an error. The server also exposes the Go runtime and process metrics of the client library.
prometheus.other: {{count}} other metric families on this server
prometheus.missing1: Status and model on a request: api_call carries the method and the route only.
prometheus.missing2: GPU utilisation, GPU temperature and CPU: use the host's own exporter for those.
prometheus.missing3: Latency percentiles: the histogram carries buckets, and Prometheus works out the percentile when you query it.
prometheus.exampleNote: The 95th percentile of request duration over 5 minutes, across all routes.
